ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions.rationale: PrismaticGem.cs:28-52 unions `player.UnlockState.CharacterCardPools` -- every UNLOCKED CHARACTER's card pool -- into a card reward's creation options. That is other-character content, which the shared contract waives explicitly ('the sim is Ironclad-only; findings about mechanics unreachable in that scope are waiver with the reason named'), and the port's own docstring draws the same parallel the source does: ColorfulPhilosophers.cs:31 gates its whole event on `CharacterCardPools.Count() > 1`. With only the Ironclad pool present the union is a no-op by construction, so this cannot change an outcome in the sim's scope -- it is not merely unported content. See guard G1 for the one residual shape and for what would make this a gap. NOTE per binding rule 7: this rationale leans on ColorfulPhilosophers.cs and Splash.cs, which this record does NOT hash.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the four early-return clauses of ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions (PrismaticGem.cs:34-49) select exactly the case the waiver above depends on -- and one of them is the residual risk
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# bails on NoCardPoolModifications, on !IsCardReward, on `options.CustomCardPool != null` and on `options.CardPools.All(p => p.IsColorless)`. The CustomCardPool bail is what keeps the relic away from narrowed pools, so single-character the union really is identity. The residual shape is a card reward whose CardPools is a NARROWER non-colorless pool supplied through CardPools rather than CustomCardPool: there the union would broaden it back to the whole character pool even with one character unlocked. The sim cannot express any of this, because it has no pool-modification hook for rewards at all -- Relic offers only modify_card_reward_options (relics/base.py:172-176), which mutates cards that have ALREADY been generated, so a fix needs a new base hook rather than a new relic method. That is why this is recorded as a dormant gap alongside the hook's waiver rather than folded into it. DORMANCY: no ported reward path builds such a pool (rewards.py generates from the Ironclad pool), and the multi-character half needs a second character. Porting a second character pool, or a reward that narrows CardPools without CustomCardPool, makes it live. Sweep C already lists ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions among the dropped hooks that have NO Relic base method and are therefore larger than a one-relic fix (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md, Sweep C's closing paragraph) -- cited, not re-derived.

guards.issue: This is audits/seam/turn_structure.json step 17's finding, not a new one: `player.py:163-167` calls modify_max_energy first and should_reset_energy second, where CombatManager.cs:641-649 evaluates ShouldPlayerResetEnergy first and only then reads MaxEnergy inside the branch it picked. Prismatic Gem is one of those pure implementations (a bare `amount + 1`), so it neither creates nor worsens the exposure; recorded here so the relic's faithful verdict is not read as a claim that the surrounding order is right.
